514→FilterChainManagerImpl::findFilterChain(const Network::ConnectionSocket& socket,\n   515→                                        const StreamInfo::StreamInfo& info) const {\n   516→  if (matcher_) For filters configured as `[A, B, C]`, decoder iteration goes A -> B -> C.\n\n- **`StreamEncoderFilters`** (lines 92-100): Uses a **reverse** iterator (`std::vector<...>::reverse_iterator`), with `begin()` returning `rbegin()` and `end()` returning `rend()`. For filters configured as `[A, B, C]`, encoder iteration goes C -> B -> A.\n\nThis ensures request/response symmetry: the first filter to see the request is the last to see the response.\n\n### Decoder filter iteration\n\n`FilterManager::decodeHeaders()` (`source/common/http/filter_manager.cc:537`) iterates through `decoder_filters_`:\n\n```cpp\nfor (; must call `continueDecoding()`/`continueEncoding()` to resume\n\nThese map to internal `IterationState` values (`source/common/http/filter_manager.h:211-218`): `Continue`, `StopSingleIteration`, `StopAllBuffer`, `StopAllWatermark`.\n\n---\n\n## Q3: Router and Upstream\n\n### Obtaining the Target Cluster and Selecting an Upstream Host\n\nThe router filter (`Router::Filter`, defined in `source/common/router/router.h:308`) is typically the last (terminal) HTTP decoder filter. Its `decodeHeaders()` method (`source/common/router/router.cc:445`) performs:\n\n1. **Route matching** (line 468): `route_ = callbacks_->route()` retrieves the cached route (already resolved by the HCM's route resolution in `ActiveStream::decodeHeaders`).\n\n2. **Route entry extraction** (line 506): `route_entry_ = route_->routeEntry()` gets the route configuration including the target cluster name.\n\n3. **Cluster lookup** (line 518-519): `cluster = config_->cm_.getThreadLocalCluster(route_entry_->clusterName())` retrieves the thread-local cluster object from the cluster manager.\n\n4. **Host selection** is deferred to `continueDecodeHeaders()` (line 714) where a connection pool is created via `createConnPool(*cluster, selected_host)` (line 724). The `Filter` class itself implements `Upstream::LoadBalancerContextBase` (line 310 of router.h), providing callbacks used by the load balancer:\n   - `computeHashKey()` - for hash-based routing (consistent hashing)\n   - `metadataMatchCriteria()` - for subset load balancing\n   - `shouldSelectAnotherHost()` - for retry host avoidance\n   - `determinePriorityLoad()` - for priority-based selection\n   - `hostSelectionRetryCount()` - maximum host selection retry attempts\n\n### UpstreamRequest and the Upstream Filter Chain\n\nAfter obtaining a connection pool, the router creates an `UpstreamRequest` (line 845-847):\n\n```cpp\nUpstreamRequestPtr upstream_request = std::make_unique<UpstreamRequest>(\n    *this, std::move(generic_conn_pool), can_send_early_data, can_use_http3, ...);\nLinkedList::moveIntoList(std::move(upstream_request), upstream_requests_);\nupstream_requests_.front()->acceptHeadersFromRouter(end_stream);\n```\n\n`UpstreamRequest` (`source/common/router/upstream_request.h:66`) manages the lifecycle of a single upstream attempt. It implements `GenericConnectionPoolCallbacks` and serves as the bridge between the router and the upstream connection.\n\n**`acceptHeadersFromRouter()`** (`source/common/router/upstream_request.cc:380`):\n1. Requests a new stream from the connection pool: `conn_pool_->newStream(this)` (line 404)\n2. Passes request headers through the upstream HTTP filter chain: `filter_manager_->decodeHeaders(...)` (line 433)\n\nThe upstream filter chain is a separate `Http::FilterManager` owned by `UpstreamRequest` (line 223 of upstream_request.h). The terminal filter in this chain is `UpstreamCodecFilter` (`source/common/router/upstream_codec_filter.h:28`), whose `decodeHeaders()` encodes the request to the upstream codec via `callbacks_->upstreamCallbacks()->upstream()->encodeHeaders(headers, end_stream)`.\n\nWhen the connection pool has a ready connection, `UpstreamRequest::onPoolReady()` (`source/common/router/upstream_request.cc:584`) stores the upstream stream handle and records the selected host.\n\n### Response Flow Back to Downstream\n\nThe response path works through several layers:\n\n1. **Upstream codec to CodecBridge**: The upstream codec decodes response bytes and delivers them to `UpstreamCodecFilter::CodecBridge` (`source/common/router/upstream_codec_filter.h:54`). `CodecBridge::decodeHeaders()` (`source/common/router/upstream_codec_filter.cc:147`) passes response headers into the upstream filter manager's encode path: `filter_.callbacks_->encodeHeaders(...)` (line 189).\n\n2. **Upstream filter chain to UpstreamRequest**: After passing through upstream filters (in reverse), `UpstreamRequest::decodeHeaders()` (`source/common/router/upstream_request.cc:267`) is called, which forwards to the router: `parent_.onUpstreamHeaders(response_code, std::move(headers), *this, end_stream)` (line 306).\n\n3. **Router to downstream filter chain**: `Filter::onUpstreamHeaders()` (`source/common/router/router.cc:1652`) processes the response:\n   - Applies header modifications (line 1658)\n   - Reports to outlier detection (line 1674-1676)\n   - Evaluates retry policy (lines 1688-1728)\n   - If this is the final response, marks `final_upstream_request_` (line 1796) and resets other hedged requests (line 1799)\n   - Forwards to the downstream HTTP filter chain: `callbacks_->encodeHeaders(std::move(headers), end_stream, ...)` (line 1804)\n\n4. **Downstream encode chain**: The `FilterManager::encodeHeaders()` iterates through encoder filters in **reverse** order (C -> B -> A), then writes to the downstream codec.\n\nThe data and trailer paths follow the same pattern:\n- `Filter::onUpstreamData()` (line 1808) -> `callbacks_->encodeData(data, end_stream)` (line 1822)\n- `Filter::onUpstreamTrailers()` (line 1825) -> `callbacks_->encodeTrailers(std::move(trailers))` (line 1846)\n\n---\n\n## Q4: Architectural Boundaries\n\n### Network-Level Filter Chain (`FilterChainManager` / `Network::FilterManagerImpl`)\n\nThe network-level filter chain operates at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP) and is defined in `source/common/network/filter_manager_impl.h:108`. `Network::FilterManagerImpl` manages two lists:\n\n- **Read filters** (`upstream_filters_` list): Iterated in FIFO order when data arrives from downstream. Filters implement `Network::ReadFilter` (`envoy/network/filter.h:240`), which provides `onData(Buffer::Instance& data, bool end_stream)` and `onNewConnection()`.\n- **Write filters** (`downstream_filters_` list): Iterated in LIFO order when data is sent downstream. Filters implement `Network::WriteFilter` (`envoy/network/filter.h:122`) with `onWrite(Buffer::Instance& data, bool end_stream)`.\n\nNetwork filters operate on **raw bytes** (`Buffer::Instance`). They have no concept of HTTP requests, headers, or streams. The scope of a network filter is the **entire connection lifetime**.\n\nThe `FilterChainManager` (`source/common/listener_manager/filter_chain_manager_impl.h:127`) sits above this - it selects *which* set of network filters to install based on connection properties (destination IP/port, SNI, ALPN, etc.). Each `FilterChain` bundles a transport socket factory (TLS configuration) and a list of network filter factories.\n\n### HTTP-Level Filter Chain (`Http::FilterManager`)\n\nThe HTTP-level filter chain operates at Layer 7 and is defined in `source/common/http/filter_manager.h:681`. `Http::FilterManager` manages:\n\n- **Decoder filters** (`decoder_filters_`): Iterated forward (A -> B -> C) for request processing. Filters implement `Http::StreamDecoderFilter` (`envoy/http/filter.h:902`) with typed methods like `decodeHeaders(RequestHeaderMap&, bool)`, `decodeData(Buffer::Instance&, bool)`, `decodeTrailers(RequestTrailerMap&)`.\n- **Encoder filters** (`encoder_filters_`): Iterated in **reverse** (C -> B -> A) for response processing. Filters implement `Http::StreamEncoderFilter` (`envoy/http/filter.h:1118`) with `encodeHeaders(ResponseHeaderMap&, bool)`, `encodeData(Buffer::Instance&, bool)`, `encodeTrailers(ResponseTrailerMap&)`.\n\nHTTP filters operate on **typed HTTP objects** (header maps, data buffers, trailer maps, metadata). The scope of an HTTP filter is a **single request/response stream** - on a multiplexed HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 connection, many HTTP filter chains run concurrently on the same underlying TCP connection.\n\n### Why They Are Separate\n\nThe separation exists for several architectural reasons:\n\n1. **Protocol generality**: The network filter layer handles any L4 protocol. Besides HCM, other network filters include TCP Proxy (`source/common/tcp_proxy/tcp_proxy.h:414`), Redis Proxy, Mongo Proxy, and others. These filters handle non-HTTP protocols at the byte level and would not benefit from HTTP-specific abstractions.\n\n2. **Multiplexing**: A single TCP connection can carry multiple concurrent HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 streams. The network filter chain runs once per connection, while HTTP filter chains run once per stream. This 1:N relationship requires separate management.\n\n3. **Layered processing**: Network filters handle connection-level concerns (rate limiting, TLS inspection, protocol detection) before the protocol is even parsed. HTTP filters handle request-level concerns (routing, authentication, header manipulation) after full HTTP semantics are available.\n\n4. **Composability**: Network filters can be stacked independently. For example, a rate-limit network filter can sit in front of HCM, or the same rate-limit filter can sit in front of a TCP proxy. The HTTP filter chain is entirely encapsulated within the HCM network filter.\n\n### How They Relate\n\nThe relationship is containment: the HTTP Connection Manager (`ConnectionManagerImpl`) is a `Network::ReadFilter` (declared at `source/common/http/conn_manager_impl.h:60-61`) that **contains** an HTTP filter chain for each stream. The flow is:\n\n```\nListener accepts TCP connection\n  -> FilterChainManager selects network filter chain\n    -> Network::FilterManagerImpl installs network filters (including HCM)\n      -> HCM::onData() receives raw bytes\n        -> HTTP codec parses bytes into HTTP frames\n          -> HCM::newStream() creates ActiveStream\n            -> Http::FilterManager creates HTTP filter chain per stream\n              -> Decoder filters process request (A -> B -> C -> Router)\n              -> Encoder filters process response (C -> B -> A -> downstream)\n```\n\nThe network filter chain is the container; the HTTP filter chain lives inside one particular network filter (the HCM).\n\n---\n\n## Evidence\n\n### Listener and Connection Acceptance\n- `source/common/listener_manager/active_tcp_listener.cc:80` - This drives the HTTP parsing state machine which will eventually call back into `ConnectionManagerImpl::newStream()` when a new HTTP stream is detected.\n\n3. **Error handling** (lines 505-519): Protocol errors, buffer floods, and overload conditions are handled, potentially closing the connection.\n\n4. **Redispatch loop** (lines 499-534): For HTTP/1.1, if the codec completes a stream and more data remains, the loop redispatches to handle pipelined requests.\n\nThe method always returns `Network::FilterStatus::StopIteration` (line 535), preventing further network filters from processing (the HCM consumes all data).\n\n---\n\n## Q2: HTTP Filter Chain Creation and Iteration\n\n### Filter Chain Creation\n\nThe HTTP filter chain is created when the first request headers arrive on a stream. The sequence is:\n\n1. The codec parses request headers and calls `ConnectionManagerImpl::newStream()` (`source/common/http/conn_manager_impl.cc:387`), which creates an `ActiveStream` (line 407).\n\n2. The codec then delivers headers to `ActiveStream::decodeHeaders()` (line 1193), which performs request processing (connection management checks, tracing setup, route resolution at line 1392).\n\n3. At line 1402-1403, the downstream filter chain is created:\n   ```cpp\n   const FilterManager::CreateChainResult create_chain_result =\n       filter_manager_.createDownstreamFilterChain();\n   ```\n\n4. `DownstreamFilterManager::createDownstreamFilterChain()` (`source/common/http/filter_manager.cc:1086`) delegates to `FilterManager::createFilterChain()` (line 1660).\n\n5. `createFilterChain()` calls `filter_chain_factory.createFilterChain(*this, options)` (line 1701) which invokes each HTTP filter factory. Each factory calls back into `FilterChainFactoryCallbacksImpl` methods:\n   - `addStreamDecoderFilter()` - wraps the filter in `ActiveStreamDecoderFilter` and appends to `decoder_filters_.entries_`\n   - `addStreamEncoderFilter()` - wraps in `ActiveStreamEncoderFilter` and appends to `encoder_filters_.entries_`\n   - `addStreamFilter()` - adds to both decoder and encoder chains\n\n6. After creation, iterator entries are initialized (lines 1668-1675).\n\n7. Finally, `filter_manager_.decodeHeaders()` is called at line 1439, which begins iterating through decoder filters.\n\n### Decoder vs. Encoder Filter Order\n\nThe two filter containers are defined in `source/common/http/filter_manager.h`:\n\n- **`StreamDecoderFilters`** (lines 73-81): Uses a forward iterator (`std::vector<...>::iterator`). For filters configured as `[A, B, C]`, decoder iteration goes A -> B -> C.\n\n- **`StreamEncoderFilters`** (lines 92-100): Uses a **reverse** iterator (`std::vector<...>::reverse_iterator`), with `begin()` returning `rbegin()` and `end()` returning `rend()`. For filters configured as `[A, B, C]`, encoder iteration goes C -> B -> A.\n\nThis ensures request/response symmetry: the first filter to see the request is the last to see the response.\n\n### Decoder filter iteration\n\n`FilterManager::decodeHeaders()` (`source/common/http/filter_manager.cc:537`) iterates through `decoder_filters_`:\n\n```cpp\nfor (; entry != decoder_filters_.end(); entry++) {\n    FilterHeadersStatus status = (*entry)->decodeHeaders(headers, (*entry)->end_stream_);\n    const auto continue_iteration = (*entry)->commonHandleAfterHeadersCallback(status, end_stream);\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\nSimilarly, `decodeData()` (line 638) and `decodeTrailers()` (line 796) iterate forward through decoder filters.\n\n### Encoder filter iteration\n\n`FilterManager::encodeHeaders()` (`source/common/http/filter_manager.cc:1225`) iterates through `encoder_filters_` (which goes in reverse due to the reverse_iterator):\n\n```cpp\nfor (; entry != encoder_filters_.end(); entry++) {\n    FilterHeadersStatus status = (*entry)->handle_->encodeHeaders(headers, end_stream);\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\nSimilarly, `encodeData()` (line 1401) and `encodeTrailers()` (line 1476) iterate in reverse through encoder filters.\n\n### Filter Return Values\n\nFilters control iteration through these return status enums (defined in `envoy/http/filter.h`):\n\n**`FilterHeadersStatus`** (line 38):\n- `Continue` (line 40): Continue to the next filter\n- `StopIteration` (line 49): Stop; filter must later call `continueDecoding()`/`continueEncoding()` to resume\n- `ContinueAndDontEndStream` (line 86): Continue iteration but convert headers-only to headers+body (delays end_stream)\n- `StopAllIterationAndBuffer` (line 98): Stop all frame types (headers, data, trailers); buffer incoming data up to the configured limit\n- `StopAllIterationAndWatermark` (line 109): Stop all frame types; apply flow control watermarks to pause upstream reads\n\n**`FilterDataStatus`** (line 129):\n- `Continue` (line 134): Continue to the next filter\n- `StopIterationAndBuffer` (line 144): Stop iteration, buffer data for later dispatch\n- `StopIterationAndWatermark` (line 155): Stop iteration, apply watermarks to pause incoming data\n- `StopIterationNoBuffer` (line 164): Stop iteration, do not buffer data\n\n**`FilterTrailersStatus`** (line 171):\n- `Continue` (line 173): Continue to the next filter\n- `StopIteration` (line 176): Stop; must call `continueDecoding()`/`continueEncoding()` to resume\n\nThese map to internal `IterationState` values (`source/common/http/filter_manager.h:211-218`): `Continue`, `StopSingleIteration`, `StopAllBuffer`, `StopAllWatermark`.\n\n---\n\n## Q3: Router and Upstream\n\n### Obtaining the Target Cluster and Selecting an Upstream Host\n\nThe router filter (`Router::Filter`, defined in `source/common/router/router.h:308`) is typically the last (terminal) HTTP decoder filter. Its `decodeHeaders()` method (`source/common/router/router.cc:445`) performs:\n\n1. **Route matching** (line 468): `route_ = callbacks_->route()` retrieves the cached route (already resolved by the HCM's route resolution in `ActiveStream::decodeHeaders`).\n\n2. **Route entry extraction** (line 506): `route_entry_ = route_->routeEntry()` gets the route configuration including the target cluster name.\n\n3. **Cluster lookup** (line 518-519): `cluster = config_->cm_.getThreadLocalCluster(route_entry_->clusterName())` retrieves the thread-local cluster object from the cluster manager.\n\n4. **Host selection** is deferred to `continueDecodeHeaders()` (line 714) where a connection pool is created via `createConnPool(*cluster, selected_host)` (line 724). The `Filter` class itself implements `Upstream::LoadBalancerContextBase` (line 310 of router.h), providing callbacks used by the load balancer:\n   - `computeHashKey()` - for hash-based routing (consistent hashing)\n   - `metadataMatchCriteria()` - for subset load balancing\n   - `shouldSelectAnotherHost()` - for retry host avoidance\n   - `determinePriorityLoad()` - for priority-based selection\n   - `hostSelectionRetryCount()` - maximum host selection retry attempts\n\n### UpstreamRequest and the Upstream Filter Chain\n\nAfter obtaining a connection pool, the router creates an `UpstreamRequest` (line 845-847):\n\n```cpp\nUpstreamRequestPtr upstream_request = std::make_unique<UpstreamRequest>(\n    *this, std::move(generic_conn_pool), can_send_early_data, can_use_http3, ...);\nLinkedList::moveIntoList(std::move(upstream_request), upstream_requests_);\nupstream_requests_.front()->acceptHeadersFromRouter(end_stream);\n```\n\n`UpstreamRequest` (`source/common/router/upstream_request.h:66`) manages the lifecycle of a single upstream attempt. It implements `GenericConnectionPoolCallbacks` and serves as the bridge between the router and the upstream connection.\n\n**`acceptHeadersFromRouter()`** (`source/common/router/upstream_request.cc:380`):\n1. Requests a new stream from the connection pool: `conn_pool_->newStream(this)` (line 404)\n2. Passes request headers through the upstream HTTP filter chain: `filter_manager_->decodeHeaders(...)` (line 433)\n\nThe upstream filter chain is a separate `Http::FilterManager` owned by `UpstreamRequest` (line 223 of upstream_request.h). The terminal filter in this chain is `UpstreamCodecFilter` (`source/common/router/upstream_codec_filter.h:28`), whose `decodeHeaders()` encodes the request to the upstream codec via `callbacks_->upstreamCallbacks()->upstream()->encodeHeaders(headers, end_stream)`.\n\nWhen the connection pool has a ready connection, `UpstreamRequest::onPoolReady()` (`source/common/router/upstream_request.cc:584`) stores the upstream stream handle and records the selected host.\n\n### Response Flow Back to Downstream\n\nThe response path works through several layers:\n\n1. **Upstream codec to CodecBridge**: The upstream codec decodes response bytes and delivers them to `UpstreamCodecFilter::CodecBridge` (`source/common/router/upstream_codec_filter.h:54`). `CodecBridge::decodeHeaders()` (`source/common/router/upstream_codec_filter.cc:147`) passes response headers into the upstream filter manager's encode path: `filter_.callbacks_->encodeHeaders(...)` (line 189).\n\n2. **Upstream filter chain to UpstreamRequest**: After passing through upstream filters (in reverse), `UpstreamRequest::decodeHeaders()` (`source/common/router/upstream_request.cc:267`) is called, which forwards to the router: `parent_.onUpstreamHeaders(response_code, std::move(headers), *this, end_stream)` (line 306).\n\n3. **Router to downstream filter chain**: `Filter::onUpstreamHeaders()` (`source/common/router/router.cc:1652`) processes the response:\n   - Applies header modifications (line 1658)\n   - Reports to outlier detection (line 1674-1676)\n   - Evaluates retry policy (lines 1688-1728)\n   - If this is the final response, marks `final_upstream_request_` (line 1796) and resets other hedged requests (line 1799)\n   - Forwards to the downstream HTTP filter chain: `callbacks_->encodeHeaders(std::move(headers), end_stream, ...)` (line 1804)\n\n4. **Downstream encode chain**: The `FilterManager::encodeHeaders()` iterates through encoder filters in **reverse** order (C -> B -> A), then writes to the downstream codec.\n\nThe data and trailer paths follow the same pattern:\n- `Filter::onUpstreamData()` (line 1808) -> `callbacks_->encodeData(data, end_stream)` (line 1822)\n- `Filter::onUpstreamTrailers()` (line 1825) -> `callbacks_->encodeTrailers(std::move(trailers))` (line 1846)\n\n---\n\n## Q4: Architectural Boundaries\n\n### Network-Level Filter Chain (`FilterChainManager` / `Network::FilterManagerImpl`)\n\nThe network-level filter chain operates at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP) and is defined in `source/common/network/filter_manager_impl.h:108`. `Network::FilterManagerImpl` manages two lists:\n\n- **Read filters** (`upstream_filters_` list): Iterated in FIFO order when data arrives from downstream. Filters implement `Network::ReadFilter` (`envoy/network/filter.h:240`), which provides `onData(Buffer::Instance& data, bool end_stream)` and `onNewConnection()`.\n- **Write filters** (`downstream_filters_` list): Iterated in LIFO order when data is sent downstream. Filters implement `Network::WriteFilter` (`envoy/network/filter.h:122`) with `onWrite(Buffer::Instance& data, bool end_stream)`.\n\nNetwork filters operate on **raw bytes** (`Buffer::Instance`). They have no concept of HTTP requests, headers, or streams. The scope of a network filter is the **entire connection lifetime**.\n\nThe `FilterChainManager` (`source/common/listener_manager/filter_chain_manager_impl.h:127`) sits above this - it selects *which* set of network filters to install based on connection properties (destination IP/port, SNI, ALPN, etc.). Each `FilterChain` bundles a transport socket factory (TLS configuration) and a list of network filter factories.\n\n### HTTP-Level Filter Chain (`Http::FilterManager`)\n\nThe HTTP-level filter chain operates at Layer 7 and is defined in `source/common/http/filter_manager.h:681`. `Http::FilterManager` manages:\n\n- **Decoder filters** (`decoder_filters_`): Iterated forward (A -> B -> C) for request processing. Filters implement `Http::StreamDecoderFilter` (`envoy/http/filter.h:902`) with typed methods like `decodeHeaders(RequestHeaderMap&, bool)`, `decodeData(Buffer::Instance&, bool)`, `decodeTrailers(RequestTrailerMap&)`.\n- **Encoder filters** (`encoder_filters_`): Iterated in **reverse** (C -> B -> A) for response processing. Filters implement `Http::StreamEncoderFilter` (`envoy/http/filter.h:1118`) with `encodeHeaders(ResponseHeaderMap&, bool)`, `encodeData(Buffer::Instance&, bool)`, `encodeTrailers(ResponseTrailerMap&)`.\n\nHTTP filters operate on **typed HTTP objects** (header maps, data buffers, trailer maps, metadata). The scope of an HTTP filter is a **single request/response stream** - on a multiplexed HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 connection, many HTTP filter chains run concurrently on the same underlying TCP connection.\n\n### Why They Are Separate\n\nThe separation exists for several architectural reasons:\n\n1. **Protocol generality**: The network filter layer handles any L4 protocol. Besides HCM, other network filters include TCP Proxy (`source/common/tcp_proxy/tcp_proxy.h:414`), Redis Proxy, Mongo Proxy, and others. These filters handle non-HTTP protocols at the byte level and would not benefit from HTTP-specific abstractions.\n\n2. **Multiplexing**: A single TCP connection can carry multiple concurrent HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 streams. The network filter chain runs once per connection, while HTTP filter chains run once per stream. This 1:N relationship requires separate management.\n\n3. **Layered processing**: Network filters handle connection-level concerns (rate limiting, TLS inspection, protocol detection) before the protocol is even parsed. HTTP filters handle request-level concerns (routing, authentication, header manipulation) after full HTTP semantics are available.\n\n4. **Composability**: Network filters can be stacked independently. For example, a rate-limit network filter can sit in front of HCM, or the same rate-limit filter can sit in front of a TCP proxy. The HTTP filter chain is entirely encapsulated within the HCM network filter.\n\n### How They Relate\n\nThe relationship is containment: the HTTP Connection Manager (`ConnectionManagerImpl`) is a `Network::ReadFilter` (declared at `source/common/http/conn_manager_impl.h:60-61`) that **contains** an HTTP filter chain for each stream. The flow is:\n\n```\nListener accepts TCP connection\n  -> FilterChainManager selects network filter chain\n    -> Network::FilterManagerImpl installs network filters (including HCM)\n      -> HCM::onData() receives raw bytes\n        -> HTTP codec parses bytes into HTTP frames\n          -> HCM::newStream() creates ActiveStream\n            -> Http::FilterManager creates HTTP filter chain per stream\n              -> Decoder filters process request (A -> B -> C -> Router)\n              -> Encoder filters process response (C -> B -> A -> downstream)\n```\n\nThe network filter chain is the container; the HTTP filter chain lives inside one particular network filter (the HCM).\n\n---\n\n## Evidence\n\n### Listener and Connection Acceptance\n- `source/common/listener_manager/active_tcp_listener.cc:80` -
